edges.description: Loss of functional AP-5 adaptor complexes directly impairs cargo sorting out of late endosomes toward the trans-Golgi network.
Loss of the AP-5 zeta subunit impairs autophagic lysosome reformation and blocks autophagic flux.
Defective late-endosomal cargo retrieval causes unretrieved substrates to accumulate within enlarged multilamellar endolysosomes.
Impaired recycling of lysosomes from autolysosomes compounds intracellular waste retention within endolysosomal compartments.
Blocked autophagic flux and neuronal waste accumulation drive age-dependent degeneration of long corticospinal tract axons.
Impaired neuronal autophagic clearance contributes to degeneration across cortical and subcortical brain regions.
Defective autophagic clearance in peripheral neurons contributes to length-dependent motor and sensory axonal degeneration.
Chronic endolysosomal storage accumulation in upper motor neurons compromises long descending corticospinal axons.
Endolysosomal storage accumulation in central nervous system neurons contributes to cortical and subcortical degeneration.
Endolysosomal storage accumulation in long peripheral motor and sensory fibers contributes to axonal polyneuropathy.
Corticospinal axon degeneration manifests on examination as pyramidal upper motor neuron signs.
Length-dependent degeneration of descending corticospinal axons produces progressive spastic paraplegia.
Loss of descending corticospinal inhibitory input causes lower-limb hypertonia and spasticity.
Disruption of descending spinal pathways controlling detrusor function causes neurogenic spastic bladder and urinary incontinence.
Degeneration of interhemispheric callosal fibers produces thinning of the corpus callosum on MRI.
Periventricular and deep cerebral white matter degeneration manifests as white matter hyperintensities on brain MRI.
Subcortical and basal ganglia neurodegeneration manifests clinically as parkinsonism in a subset of patients.
Cortical and fronto-callosal neurodegeneration causes cognitive impairment or intellectual disability in complicated SPG48.
Brainstem and subcortical cerebellar-pathway neurodegeneration produces limb and gait ataxia in complicated SPG48.
Basal ganglia and subcortical motor circuit degeneration causes focal or limb dystonia in a subset of patients.
Peripheral motor and sensory nerve fiber degeneration manifests clinically as sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy.

Ap5z1 knockout cells and neurons exhibit impaired autophagic flux and defective recycling of lysosomes from autolysosomes, with accumulation of autophagosomes, autolysosomes, and intracellular waste in vivo.
edges.limitations: Constitutive murine Ap5z1 loss models complete null deficiency in mouse neurons rather than patient-specific missense or truncating alleles in human neuronal subtypes.

edges.description: Ap5z1 knockout mice develop progressive age-dependent degeneration of corticospinal tract axons.
edges.limitations: Rodent corticospinal tracts are shorter and have different descending motor projections than human pyramidal tracts, resulting in milder motor disability than human spastic paraplegia.

evidence.reference_title: Early Diagnosis of AP5Z1/SPG48 Spastic Paraplegia: Case Report and Review of the Literature.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in AP5Z1, which are associated with spastic paraplegia type 48 (SPG48), are extremely rare and seldom described in children.We report the clinical, radiologic, and molecular studies performed in a child harboring novel biallelic mutations in AP5Z1.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in AP5Z1 abolish or deplete the AP-5 zeta subunit and destabilize associated AP-5 subunits (including mu5), disrupting assembly and clathrin-independent cargo-adaptor activity of the AP-5/SPG11/SPG15 endolysosomal coat-like complex.

evidence.reference_title: Early Diagnosis of AP5Z1/SPG48 Spastic Paraplegia: Case Report and Review of the Literature.

nodes.description: Defective late-endosomal sorting and lysosome homeostasis cause patient cells and neurons to accumulate enlarged multilamellar endolysosomes filled with aberrant storage material organized as whorls, striated belts, and fingerprint bodies, defining a trafficking-driven lysosomal storage defect.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of AP-5 results in accumulation of aberrant endolysosomes: defining a new type of lysosomal storage disease.
evidence.snippet: Using ultrastructural analysis, we show that these patient-derived lines consistently exhibit abundant multilamellar structures that are positive for markers of endolysosomes and are filled with aberrant storage material organized as exaggerated multilamellar whorls, striated belts and 'fingerprint bodies'.

nodes.description: Mice carrying constitutive disruption of murine Ap5z1 (orthologous to human AP5Z1) develop age-dependent degeneration of corticospinal tract axons accompanied by impaired autophagic flux, defective lysosome recycling from autolysosomes, and progressive accumulation of autophagosomes, autolysosomes, and intracellular waste in neurons.
